fieldframe.status.arcana_no_condition.fi: Move it high up, deep down, under open sky, into rain or the Nether.
fieldframe.status.arcana_no_essentia.fix: Put a jar with a burnable aspect in front of this face.
fieldframe.status.arcana_no_essentia_sou: Place a jar or reservoir against this face.
fieldframe.status.arcana_no_wand.fix: Put a wand into the input storage.
fieldframe.status.arcana_thin_aura: The aura here is too thin to tap.
fieldframe.status.arcana_thin_aura.fix: Wait for it to recover, or tune floor_fraction lower.
fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_sword.empty: Not enough charge to switch on
module.fieldframe_arcana.aura_tap.desc: Draws vis from the chunk's aura into RF; stops before the aura falls below a share of its base.
module.fieldframe_arcana.essentia_dynamo: Burns essentia from the vessel in front of it into RF, one point at a time; leaks a little flux.
module.fieldframe_arcana.etheric_crusher: Crushes raw ore into doubled crushed ore, with a chance at a vis crystal.
module.fieldframe_arcana.flux_scrubber.d: Pays RF to pull flux out of the chunk's aura and packs it into vitium crystals.
module.fieldframe_arcana.node_cradle.des: Draws vis from a vis relay network or the chunk's aura and holds it for the Vis Charger to use.
module.fieldframe_arcana.primal_condense: Spends RF to condense vis crystals where the world favours their aspect: height, depth, rain, sky, the Nether.
module.fieldframe_arcana.vis_charger.des: Charges wands from its input storage with vis bought with RF; full wands go to its output.
research.fieldframe_arcana.arc.stage_0: A spell is a pattern the vis flows through. Wire one part of it to a cell and part of the flow can come from the cell.
research.fieldframe_arcana.arc.stage_1: The Arc is a spell part that fits in any focus. A spell that holds it pays half its vis cost (unless tuned) in RF from energy items in the inventory, if they can cover it. Without enough RF the spell costs its full vis.
research.fieldframe_arcana.arc.title: Arc
research.fieldframe_arcana.aura_tap.stag: The dynamo burns essentia. The aura itself is thinner fuel, but it is everywhere and it grows back.

The Aura Tap draws vis from the chunk's aura and turns it into RF for the chassis. It never draws the aura below a share of its base (half, unless tuned), so the chunk recovers; then it waits. The faster the chassis, the faster it draws.
research.fieldframe_arcana.essentia_dyna: A jar of ignis is a jar of heat waiting to be spent. If a module could sip from it one point at a time, the chassis' coils would do the rest.

The Essentia Dynamo faces a jar, a reservoir or any vessel that offers its essentia, and burns one point at a time into the chassis' RF buffer, taking whichever aspect in front of it is worth most. Potentia, machina and ignis pay best; ordo is clean but weak; vitium pays handsomely and fouls the air. Every point burned leaves a little flux in the chunk. It stops when the buffer is full and can be switched by a signal; its 'active' output says when it burns.
research.fieldframe_arcana.etheric_crush: A crusher grinds ore to grit. Grind it with salis mundus on the rollers and the grit gives up a little of its aspect as well.

The Etheric Crusher is a Fieldframe processor: it takes from its input storage and doubles raw ores into crushed ore like the engineers' crusher, with a chance at a vis crystal of the ore's aspect. Blaze rods and phantom membranes give up ignis and aer. Its recipes are the etherealize family, so datapacks can add more.
research.fieldframe_arcana.field_drill.s: Thaumium holds an edge the way nothing else does, and a cell turns a bit faster than any arm.

The Thaumium Field Drill digs stone and earth at diamond level, never wears out, and spends RF per block instead. Sneak-use switches its mode: normal; area, which breaks a 3x3 face; and refining, which smelts what it digs on the spot, paying a little RF and vis from the aura for each item. Empty, it digs no better than a fist.
research.fieldframe_arcana.field_lens.st: Goggles of Revealing show the aspects of things. An engineer would rather see what a machine is doing, and a thaumaturge would rather see the air thin before it runs out.

The Field Lens is a pair of Goggles of Revealing wired to a cell. Worn, it reveals aspects and nodes like the goggles, and grants night vision while it has charge. Sneak and it reads out what you look at: a chassis' RF and the state of every module on it, or else the vis, flux and base of the aura around you. It spends a little RF every second; charge it at any Fieldframe charger.
research.fieldframe_arcana.field_saw.sta: The drill's motor would turn a chain as well as a bit.

The Thaumium Field Saw cuts wood, leaves and wool, never wears out, and spends RF per block. In felling mode (sneak-use to switch) a log brings down every log joined to it, for one vis from the aura per tree; hold sneak while cutting to take a single log.
research.fieldframe_arcana.flux_scrubber: What the dynamo leaks, the chassis can take back, if it is willing to pay.
The Flux Scrubber pulls flux out of the chunk's aura, paying RF for every point, and packs it into vitium crystals in its output storage. It idles when the air is clean.
research.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_boot: The traveller's boots are light; with a cell in the heel they need not tire either.
Galvanic Boots step up full blocks and run faster while they have charge, paying RF for every metre walked. Sneak-use them in hand to switch them off and on.
If the sword can throw an arc a few blocks, a bow can carry one much farther.

The Galvanic Thaumium Bow never wears out. While it has charge it needs no arrows: each shot spends RF and fires a bolt that draws twice as fast, hits harder and arcs to the nearest hostile mob near whatever it strikes. Bolts can't be picked up. Empty, it shoots your arrows like any bow. Sneak-use switches it to quick fire: while charged, every use looses a full-power bolt at once for a little more RF, with a short pause between shots.
research.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_jetp: The wings need a running start and a fall. Two nozzles and a heavy cell need neither.

The Galvanic Jetpack is worn as a chestplate. Hold jump to rise, steering with the movement keys, for RF every tick. Sneak-use it in hand to cycle on, hover and off: in hover mode you sink slowly instead of falling when you let go of jump, for a little RF, and sneaking drops you normally. It never lets fall damage build up. Bolt a thaumium chestplate over it and it becomes the Armored Galvanic Jetpack: it flies the same, holds more charge and guards you like the chestplate, even when its cell is empty.
If a module can buy vis with RF, a wand could carry its own bargain with it: a greatwood core, wound in mithril and signal alloy.

A wand on a Galvanic rod holds as much as one on a primal rod but never draws on the aura. Instead, while you carry it, it buys vis from any energy item in your inventory (a charged cell or battery) and gives it to its emptiest primal. Assemble it with any caps like any other rod.
research.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_staf: Two galvanic rods and a cell between them: a staff that pays for itself.
A staff on the Galvanic core holds 175 vis and refills like the Galvanic rod, from energy items you carry, but buys its vis in bigger pulses. Assemble it with caps like any staff.
research.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_swor: A thaumium blade carries vis well. It carries current better.
The Galvanic Thaumium Sword never wears out. While it has charge, every hit spends RF for extra damage and jumps as an arc to the nearest hostile mob close to your target. Empty, it is still a sword.
research.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_thau: The engineers' chassis are honest machines: modules on a frame, an RF buffer, lanes of goods. Nothing in them knows the aspects. Yet essentia is stored effort, and effort is what a dynamo makes.

A Fieldframe module can be built to speak to Thaumaturge's vessels and wands. It still keeps the engineers' rule: it only touches the block in front of its own face, and nothing carries vis or RF over a distance. What the module spends or burns, the aura notices.
research.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_wing: An elytra glides. Give it a cell and a little thrust and it flies.

Galvanic Wings are a chestplate that glides like an elytra. While you glide with them switched on, they push you along your gaze up to a top speed, spending RF every tick; no rockets needed. Sneak-use in hand switches the thrust off and on.
research.fieldframe_arcana.node_cradle.s: A relay network carries vis from crystal to crystal. A chassis could hold a cup under it.

The Vis Cradle draws a little vis each tick from a vis relay network that reaches the block in front of it, one primal after another, or from the chunk's aura when no relay does. It holds the vis for the chassis, and a Vis Charger on the same chassis drinks from the cradle first and pays RF only for the rest. Jarred nodes no longer feed it; any left in its storage can be taken back out.
research.fieldframe_arcana.primal_conden: Each primal gathers where the world favours it: air high up, earth deep down, water in the rain.

The Primal Condenser spends RF to condense a vis crystal into its output storage, but only where the world favours that aspect: aer above y 100 (faster in a thunderstorm), terra below y 40, aqua in rain, ignis in the Nether, ordo under a clear day sky, perditio under the night sky. Set it to one aspect or let it make whatever the place allows.
research.fieldframe_arcana.vis_charger.s: A wand drinks vis from the air, and the air runs thin. A chassis has no such shortage of RF. Could a module turn the one into the other, without asking the aura at all?

The Vis Charger takes a wand from its input storage and pours vis into it, always into the emptiest primal, paying RF from the chassis buffer for every drop. A full wand moves to its output storage. A faster chassis tier charges faster, for the same RF per vis. It never draws on the aura.
The galvanic rod buys vis before you need it. A silverwood core, wired through, could pay at the moment of casting instead, and pay half of it in RF.

A wand on a Voltaic core holds as much as a silverwood one. Whenever vis leaves it, for a spell, a focus, the workbench or anything else, half of it is put back and paid in RF from a buffer in the wand. The buffer fills itself from energy items you carry. When the buffer runs dry the wand pays in full, like any other. Assemble it with any caps.
research.fieldframe_arcana.voltaic_staff: Two voltaic cores and a primal charm between them.
A staff on the Voltaic core holds 250 vis and pays half of every draw in RF like the wand core, from a buffer two and a half times as large. Assemble it with caps like any staff.
spell.fieldframe_arcana.arc.desc: Pays half of the spell's vis cost in RF from a charged energy item.
spell.fieldframe_arcana.arc.name: Arc
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.armored_galvan: Thaumium plating: armours like a thaumium chestplate, charged or not
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.field_drill: Spends RF per block; area mode digs 3x3; refining smelts drops
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.field_lens: Reveals aspects; night vision while charged; sneak to read chassis or aura
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.field_saw: Spends RF per block; felling mode fells whole trees
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_bow: Charged: shoots RF bolts that arc to a nearby hostile mob, no arrows needed
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_jetpa: Hold jump to rise; sneak-use to cycle on, hover and off
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_sword: Use to switch on: hits then spend RF for extra damage and arc to a nearby hostile mob
Active: drains RF while switched on
tooltip.fieldframe_arcana.galvanic_wings: Glides; thrust along your gaze while charged
